key_insight: Process-zone condensation is exact relative to the full cell discretisation while the eliminated matrix region remains elastic, retaining cohesive interfaces and process-zone plasticity without training.
engineering_relevance: The method can accelerate FE² analysis of composite debonding and matrix plasticity without sacrificing full-cell accuracy, but speed gains depend on the material and retained-zone size.
method: Eliminate the linear-elastic cell remainder using a Schur complement.
Recover macroscopic stress and consistent tangent through influence matrices.
Check the eliminated region once per increment by back-substitution and expand the retained zone when needed.
evidence_signal: Eight of nine 2D paths matched full-cell stress and tangent to 1e-11, with the ninth flagged; aggregate 2D speed-up was 3.3× excluding setup and checks, while plate-level FE² was 1.51× faster for glass/polypropylene but slower for glass/epoxy.
watch_item: Exactness requires the eliminated region to remain elastic; zone expansion, active-set changes and adaptation costs can erase computational savings, as observed in certified 3D cases.
paper_title: Process-zone condensation: a discretization-exact reduced cell model for FE$^2$ analysis of composites with fibre-matrix debonding and matrix plasticity
